# Build Candidate D — Hangar War (the outer loop)

Follow-on to **We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)**, whose deliverable
(`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`) the producer reviewed and closed by choosing
**Candidate D — Hangar War** on 2026-10-29 (`discovered-from:AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC`).
This item turns that chosen design into a playable, shippable build. The design
rationale, comparison and the agreed adjustments live in
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D) and GDD §8; they are the
requirements of record for this item.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want my runs to add up to a war I can win — a hangar worth
defending, a ring of hexes around it, and weapons I discover by beating the bosses
that wield them — so that losing a run costs me a ship and its salvage, not my
progress, and so that "beating the boss" is a milestone on the way to holding the
ring rather than the end of everything.

As the producer, I want Candidate D shipped in the order the design recommends —
**Candidate B's MVP (hangar economy) first, then the first hex ring** — so that if
the ring disappoints in play, the hangar stands alone as a complete outer loop and
no work is wasted.

## Scope (from the chosen design)

**Two outer-loop progression axes running together:**
1. **The war on the map** — a hex grid whose first **ring of six hexes** surrounds
   the hangar; which hexes are held, which hold a defending bot, and how aggressive
   the frontier is.
2. **The range of the fleet** — the hangar: hulls, starting weapons, loadouts and
   permanent modifiers bought with banked salvage.

**The capture cycle:** attack a **weak** neighbouring hex → collect salvage →
defeat its **boss** → receive a **new kind of power-up or weapon** into the hangar
→ **leave a bot** flying one of your hulls to defend the hex.

**The frontier:** between runs the AI's border aggression rises and it can
**retake** a held hex unless the player defeats the attacking neighbour. A lost
*run* is still final (ship and unbanked salvage gone); the hangar never is.
Hex defence, mineral accrual and the aggression tick are **algorithmic
resolutions over stored strength numbers** — no live simulated battle.

**Entry surface (producer decision 2026-10-30, Q1 = a):** the hangar war is
reached from its **own top-level menu entry**; **Play Game keeps running the
shipped classic campaign** exactly as today and **Continue — Level N keeps
resuming the arcade run checkpoint**. The two modes share the run code
(`PlayScene` + shared core) but never share session or checkpoint state — a
hex deployment cannot overwrite the arcade checkpoint, and vice versa.

## Agreed design adjustments (2026-10-29 producer review — requirements)

1. **Ring timing is an evening's play, not a grind.** MVP (one ring, six hexes)
   targets **40–60 minutes** for a semi-skilled player: 6 × ≈5-minute
   deployments (≈30 min) plus build/salvage time and a few losses. **Ring 2 is
   larger — 12 hexes**, ≈60 minutes of deployments plus 10–40 minutes of builds
   and losses (~70–100 min). Later rings grow again (ring *n* holds 6*n* hexes),
   so the campaign gets progressively longer, not repetitive.
2. **Boss and weapon strengths are known ahead (MVP).** Before committing to a
   hex the player can see what its boss is, what it is strong/weak against, and
   which hex grants which weapon — enabling deliberate strategy ("take that hex → I
   get the weapon that counters the boss threatening my home hex"). Going beyond
   strategic weapon grants is **out of scope for the MVP**; it is the backlog below.
3. **One hex holds the new weapon — and it is the hardest in the ring.** The other
   five hexes grant upgrades/strength. Players may rush the hard hex and push into
   the next ring (risking losses) or grind the weaker hexes and secure the ring
   first — **different play styles must all be viable** (strategists, grinders,
   completers).
4. **Starting kit clarification.** The *fleet* starts minimal (one basic hull, one
   starting weapon, no hangar modifiers), but the *run* keeps the shipped middle
   loop in full: the six shared loadout slots (any mix of power-up and weapon
   kinds) plus the two slot-free kinds, **Extra Life** and **Mystery UFO**. Do not
   strip the shipped in-run variety to create the outer loop's scarcity.
5. **Post-MVP mitigation backlog (design captured, not MVP):** special missions
   with special rewards (e.g. a new hull type with extra hit points or extra
   upgrade bays), upgraded bots with special skills that are more effective
   against certain enemy/boss types, and further variety so the ring is never a
   six-chore checklist.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hangar slice first (Candidate B's MVP).** Banked salvage (minerals + mini-boss
   cores at the existing checkpoint moments), a persistent hangar with one extra
   hull, three unlockable starting weapons, one permanent modifier, and a
   deployment/loadout selector; losing a run forfeits only that run's unbanked
   salvage.
2. **One hex ring.** A hex-grid map screen with the hangar at the centre and a ring
   of six hexes, each showing held/unheld, aggression, its boss, its granted
   weapon/upgrade and any pending attack; ring growth is data-driven **and ring 2
   (12 hexes) is playable in this build**, generated from hex definitions
   (producer decision 2026-10-30, Q3 = a).
3. **Capture cycle.** Taking a hex = a normal run at that hex's aggression, ending
   in the hex boss; defeating the boss banks salvage, grants the hex's weapon or
   upgrade into the hangar, and lets the player leave a bot flying a chosen hull.
   **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held** (producer decision
   2026-10-30, Q2 = a); the massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state
   are deferred, see *Out of scope*.
4. **Algorithmic defence + frontier tick.** A pure resolver decides holds/falls from
   stored numbers (defender rating vs attacking force × aggression); one frontier
   tick between runs raises border aggression and can retake a hex; the defence
   report shows the numbers that produced every result.
5. **Boss-granted discovery.** A hex boss demonstrates the weapon it grants; the
   entry appears in the hangar only after the boss is defeated (Rule 2), with the
   six-slot, Extra Life and Mystery UFO behaviour of the shipped run unchanged
   (Rule 1 clarification).
6. **Known-ahead intel, visible.** Hex bosses, their weaknesses and the weapon each
   hex grants are readable before the player commits to a deployment.
7. **Timing targets.** One-ring MVP is completable in 40–60 minutes by a
   semi-skilled player; ring 2 (12 hexes) lands at ≈70–100 minutes; the timing is
   recorded in the GDD and measured with the headless eval arena
   (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` per-run durations, summed per ring).
8. **Playstyles supported.** A rush through the weapon hex into the next ring, and a
   full grind of the ring before pushing, are both viable and neither is strictly
   dominant; the difficulty curve makes the aggressive line riskier but faster.
9. **Gym coverage and parity.** Hangar economy, defence resolver and frontier clock
   ship as pure logic exercised in a `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` scene; any new hull,
   weapon or bot behaviour runs the **same code** in gym and game (AGENTS.md
   gym↔game parity, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated).
10. **Attract mode never stalls.** The demo bot traverses or skips the map, hangar
    and defence report (auto-pick weakest hex, auto-buy cheapest useful unlock) and
    there is no live defence battle to stall in.
11. **Persistence.** One versioned `localStorage` key for hangar + ring under GDD
    §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend, injectable store), with a migration
    note; a partial ring is never discarded.
12. **Additive entry surface.** The main menu gains a **Hangar War** entry;
    **Play Game still starts the shipped classic 10-level campaign** and
    **Continue — Level N still resumes the arcade run checkpoint**, with no
    shared session state between the modes (producer decision 2026-10-30,
    Q1 = a).
13. **Build and full suite green**, and the docs/code comments updated.

## Out of scope

- Candidate A's region graph, faction simulation and home-world search; Candidates
  B and C as separate builds (B's MVP is the first slice of this item).
- Post-MVP mitigations beyond known-ahead intel (special missions, upgraded bots) —
  design captured in the candidates document, scheduled later.
- **The ring's massed counter-attack on the hangar and the hangar-falls lose
  state.** Deferred by producer decision (2026-10-30, Q2 = a): the MVP's ring
  win is "all six hexes held". Tracked for later by **AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK**.
- Any backend, or a real-time (simulated) hex defence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — extend or sit alongside for the outer-loop payload.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — reuse (scores, hex aggression → curve).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/` — deployment entry, no divergent copy.
- new: hangar/hex map scenes, `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar`, pure resolver + frontier clock modules and their tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `README.md`.

## Dependencies

- Builds on the completed design deliverable AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC (chosen Candidate D).
- Overlaps the attract-bot framework AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4 (traversal requirement) and the checkpoint save/resume AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51 (persistence precedent).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** Candidate D's design decisions of record are the ones recorded in
  AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC's AC16 record and GDD §8; changing them is a producer call.
- **Risk — the frontier treadmill:** AI retakes hexes faster than a casual player can
  hold them. Mitigation: every tick is answerable, and the numbers are shown.
- **Risk — two progressions, twice the bookkeeping.** Mitigation: one screen holds
  map and hangar, one click apart.
- **Risk — power creep** trivialises hexes; mitigation: ring depth raises difficulty
  and each weapon arrives only after being beaten.

## Existing state (repository survey, dev @ `0787ab6a`)

- **No outer-loop code exists yet.** A repo-wide search of `src/` for
  `hangar`, `hexGrid`, `HexRing` and salvage banking finds **nothing in
  production code** — Candidate D is design-only today
  (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D, GDD §8). Nothing but the
  conventions below constrains the new modules' shape.
- **Persistence precedents to copy, not reinvent:** `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`
  (v2 payload, `CHECKPOINT_STORAGE_KEY`, injectable `CheckpointStorage`,
  defensive parse → `null`, field-presence migration),
  `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/core/settingsStore.ts` and
  `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` (versioned corrupt-safe blob with a bundled
  baseline). GDD §6.6 lists the shipped keys (`ai_hell_leaderboard`,
  `ai_hell_settings`, `ai_hell_checkpoint`, `ai_hell_lastSession`); the outer
  loop's `ai_hell_hangar_war` is a fifth key under the same rules.
- **Difficulty reuse:** `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is consumed through
  `src/core/difficultyScaling.ts`, `difficultySequencer.ts` and
  `levelScaling.ts`; a hex's aggression should select/perturb those curves
  rather than introduce a second scaling system.
- **Entry surface:** `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` exposes Play Game,
  Continue — Level N (only when a usable checkpoint exists), Leaderboard,
  Settings, Help and the dev-only Gym Scene Index. There is **no mode
  selector** today, and Play Game deliberately clears the checkpoint.
- **Gym surface:** 14 scenes under `src/scenes/gym/` plus the generic
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, registered in `GymIndex`.
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` fails if a gym scene has no row in
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` pins
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`, so two new gym scenes imply updates to both.
- **Attract bot:** `src/ai/` (botDecision, botSnapshot, botHumanLike,
  framework/competent, eval arena) and `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`
  exist, but the demo boots straight into `PlayScene` — **no scene-to-scene
  menu traversal is shipped today**, so AC10 is new behaviour rather than a
  reuse.
- **Timing measurement is already feasible without new instrumentation:**
  `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` runs headless per-level and full-campaign simulations
  and reports `durationSeconds` / `ticksSimulated`, so a ring's play time can be
  measured against the bot rather than guessed.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** Hangar economy, defence resolver and
  frontier clock are pure modules consumed by both the game and a
  `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` scene; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`,
  and `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` rejects a duplicated helper body.
- **No backend, `localStorage` only** (GDD §6.6), behind an injectable store so
  a future backend can replace it.
- **The shipped run must not regress:** six shared loadout slots, Extra Life,
  Mystery UFO, checkpoint Continue, leaderboard and settings all keep working
  unchanged.
- **One versioned key for hangar + ring**, so a defence result can never be
  written without the hangar state it depends on; a partial ring is never
  discarded.
- **Warehouse rules:** agent-initiated test runs go through `/skill:test`;
  `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the ship skill and is not edited here.
- **Documentation of record:** GDD §8, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (build
  status), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and `README.md`.

## Clarifications and assumptions (intake, 2026-10-30)

Three scope decisions were **answered by the producer on 2026-10-30** and are
recorded in the Appendix: **Q1 = a** (additive Hangar War menu entry, Play Game
unchanged), **Q2 = a** (ring secured = all six hexes held; the hangar assault
and hangar-falls lose state deferred to AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK) and **Q3 = a**
(ring 2 playable with generated hex definitions and headless timing). Nothing
else in the brief is ambiguous; the following assumptions are recorded rather
than asked:

- **A1 — Timing method (assumption).** AC7's "measured against the bot where
  feasible" resolves to the existing headless eval arena
  (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`), summing deployment durations for a ring rather than
  adding new instrumentation.
- **A2 — Aggression → difficulty (assumption).** A hex's aggression selects or
  perturbs a row of `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing scaling
  modules; no second difficulty system is introduced.
- **A3 — Intel is static-per-hex (assumption).** Boss identity, weaknesses and
  granted weapon are properties of the hex definition, so they are readable
  without a run and need no scouting system.
- **A4 — Defence report is post-tick, not live (assumption).** The report is
  generated from the resolver's per-tick output; no battle simulation, and the
  defending bot is never flown (design of record).
- **A5 — Ring content authoring is data, not scenes (assumption).** Hex
  definitions (coordinates, boss, grant, aggression, ring membership) are CSV
  or JSON data under `src/data/`, matching the existing CSV-seed pattern, so
  ring 2 is a data change plus generator support.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `hangar`, `salvage`, `hex`, `faction`, `outer loop`, `loadout`, `hull`
and `persistence`. The only overlapping items are the **completed design
deliverables** (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC, AH-0MVRNJ0SL000RNHR,
AH-0MVTE4EOS008RMQ7) which this item builds on — no completed or open item
implements any hangar, ring, defence resolver or frontier clock, so there is no
duplicate to close or trim.

## Additional risks (intake review)

- **Risk — scope creep into the post-MVP backlog** (special missions, upgraded
  bots with skills, hex personalities, contracts, ring landmarks): all are out of
  scope here; capture them as `discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE` items rather
  than growing this build.
- **Risk — two new gym scenes drift from the game:** mitigation is the parity
  guard trio (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md` rows, `gymParityDocs.test.ts`,
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`), not review discipline alone.
- **Risk — a “hangar war” mode quietly forks the run:** mitigation: the
  deployment uses `PlayScene`/shared core with only aggression-driven inputs,
  and the equivalence test rejects a copied helper body.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVTE4EOS008RMQ7** – Add Candidate D (Hangar War) and the discovery-progression rules to the outer-loop candidates document (completed)
- **AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC** – We need an outer loop (completed)
- **AH-0MVRNJ0SL000RNHR** – Author the three outer-loop candidate outlines, comparison and recommendation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: 0mvnssy9l001p1cc, accrual, add, adjustments, again (+385 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvcrbtnf000dk51, 0mvnssy9l001p1cc, ac16, accrual, add (+373 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvnssy9l001p1cc, ac16, acceptance, add, again (+326 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (intake 2026-10-30)

Recorded per the shared interview contract; no answers received yet, so each
entry is marked **OPEN QUESTION** with the agent's recommended option. This
Appendix is idempotent — a re-run updates these entries rather than adding new
ones.

- **Q1 (entry surface).** How does the player reach the hex map, and what
  happens to the shipped arcade run?
  - (a) **New top-level "Hangar War" menu entry**; Play Game stays the classic
    10-level run exactly as today; Continue applies to arcade runs only (or to
    both, stated explicitly).
  - (b) Play Game becomes the hangar-war campaign entry and the classic run is
    demoted to a secondary menu item.
  - (c) The hangar war replaces Play Game; the classic run is reachable only
    from the dev gym index.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — additive entry keeps the shipped run (and its
    checkpoint/leaderboard semantics) untouched, matches the design's "the run
    is unchanged" claim, and is the smallest blast radius.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (a)** — a new top-level **Hangar War** menu
    entry; Play Game stays the classic 10-level run and Continue keeps resuming
    the arcade checkpoint. Source: interactive reply, session
    `herdr-1793324074-975548-23609`; recorded as AC13 and in *Scope*.
- **Q2 (ring win / hangar lose in MVP).** Candidate D's *States* section
  defines a ring win as "all six hexes held **and the AI's massed
  counter-attack on the hangar repelled**", and a campaign loss as "the hangar
  falls". The AC list only requires capture, defence and frontier tick. Which
  of these is MVP?
  - (a) **Ring secured = all six hexes held**; the massed hangar assault and the
    hangar-falls lose state are deferred (ring 2 simply opens).
  - (b) Add an **algorithmic hangar assault**: when the ring completes, one
    resolver pass decides win/lose from stored numbers; a loss restarts the ring
    (hangar state kept).
  - (c) Add a **scripted assault deployment** (a full run) as the ring's finale.
  - **Recommended: (b)** — it closes the win/lose loop with a pure resolver (no
    new gameplay, no stall risk) and keeps MVP's cost close to (a) while
    honouring the design's stated win state.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (a)** — the ring is secured when all six
    hexes are held; the massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state
    are deferred and tracked by **AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK** (created from this
    intake). Source: interactive reply, session `herdr-1793324074-975548-23609`;
    recorded in AC3 and *Out of scope*.
- **Q3 (ring 2 in this build).** AC2 wants ring growth data-driven "so ring 2
  can be 12 hexes"; AC7 names a ring-2 timing target of ≈70–100 minutes. Is ring 2
  playable in this build?
  - (a) **Ring 2 playable** — the generator emits 12 hexes with generated hex
    definitions, and its timing is measured with the headless arena.
  - (b) Ring 2 supported by the generator and unit-tested, but no authored ring-2
    content or timing validation in this build.
  - (c) Ring 2 playable plus ring 3+ locked behind a "campaign continues" placeholder.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it is the cheapest way to *prove* AC2's data-driven
    claim and AC7's ring-2 target, and generated definitions keep the content
    cost small.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): (a)** — ring 2 is playable: the generator
    emits its 12 hexes from generated definitions and the ring-2 timing target is
    validated headlessly. Source: interactive reply, session
    `herdr-1793324074-975548-23609`; recorded in AC2 and AC7.
- **Q4 (timing evidence).** Is headless-arena measurement sufficient evidence for
  the 40–60-minute and 70–100-minute budgets, or is a recorded human playtest
  required before sign-off?
  - Evidence: `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` already reports `durationSeconds` per
    simulated run, so the mechanism exists.
  - **Answer (assumption A1):** headless arena is sufficient for the recorded
    target; a human playtest is desirable but not a gate. Recorded as an
    assumption, not an open question.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-30 — plan session (agent `Map`)**: decomposed the epic into **15 child
  items in two shippable phases**, matching the design's shipping order ("ship it
  in B's shape first"):
  - **Phase A — hangar slice (Candidate B's MVP), shippable alone:** A1 harness +
    `GymHangar`, A2 versioned store, A3 salvage banking, A4 hangar economy, A5
    hangar scene/loadout selector, A6 Hangar War menu entry + mode separation +
    deployment, A7 end-to-end verification gate (also lands the phase-A docs).
  - **Phase B — first ring (plus ring 2):** B1 harness + `GymHexWar`, B2 hex ring
    model/generator/definitions, B3 defence resolver + frontier clock, B4 hex map
    with known-ahead intel, B5 capture cycle (hex boss, boss-granted discovery,
    defending bot, ring secured), B6 defence report + attract-mode traversal, B7
    ring timing/playstyle validation, B8 documentation of record.
  - Dependencies are wired with `wl dep add` (test/verification items first; B1
    gated behind A7 so the hangar slice is proven before the ring starts).
  - Acceptance-criteria coverage verified with the shared tree-coverage review:
    **100 % of the 13 epic ACs covered**, no conflicts.
  - No new questions were needed beyond the answers already recorded at intake.

### Appendix: plan decisions (2026-10-30)

No interview round was required — the three scope questions were answered by the
producer on 2026-10-30 (Q1 = a, Q2 = a, Q3 = a, recorded above) and intake's
assumptions A1–A5 remain valid. The following planning decisions are recorded so
the decomposition is auditable; none changes scope.

- **D1 — two shippable phases, in the design's order.** Phase A is Candidate B's
  MVP (a complete outer loop on its own); Phase B adds the first ring and ring 2.
  Matches `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` *Recommendation* ("Ship it in B's shape
  first … if the ring disappoints, B stands alone").
- **D2 — test/verification items come first.** A1 and B1 land fixtures, fakes and
  the gym scenes (with tests) before economy/ring code; A7 and B7 are explicit
  verification gates. Every implementation item also writes its tests first.
- **D3 — no new gameplay code paths for grants.** A hangar starting weapon and a
  hex boss's granted weapon are config variants on the shipped weapon/boss paths,
  so the parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) stays green.
- **D4 — documentation per phase.** A7 publishes the hangar-slice specification
  (so phase A is a vertical slice through code, tests and docs); B8 publishes the
  ring specification and refreshes the parity/build-status docs.
- **D5 — ring 2 is generated, not authored.** B2 emits ring 2's 12 hexes from the
  same definitions as ring 1 (Q3 = a); no ring-3 content is authored.
- **OPEN QUESTION: none.** Nothing in the plan requires a producer decision before
  implementation starts.

## Gap closure (2026-11-01, audit follow-up)

The audit of this epic (2026-11-01) returned **Ready to close: No** with two gaps.
Both were closed as children of this epic, each implemented in its own worktree
and pushed to `dev`:

- **AC5 — boss-granted discovery.** The hex boss now **wields** the weapon it
  grants: `AH-0MVXSGXF4000GDRQ` (commit `6885ca4e4`) adds a default-preserving
  `BossConfig.demonstratedWeapon` hook so a hex boss opens the encounter with
  the granted weapon's own volley (fan offsets, bullet colour and shape resolved
  from the shared `src/utils/weapons.ts` catalogue through the pure
  `hexBossDemonstration`), with the body colour kept as a secondary tell; later
  phases keep the shipped patterns, and the classic campaign boss is unchanged.
- **AC8 — playstyles supported.** The rush line is now **playable**:
  `AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0` (commit `72ac25b32`) opens the next ring when the
  current ring's **capstone** (`weaponHex`) is held (`isRingOpenable`), carries
  the hexes a rush skips (held state, defenders, rising aggression) instead of
  discarding them, and makes `isRingSecured` ring-scoped. Q2 = a is unchanged —
  *ring secured* still means every hex of the ring held, and the massed hangar
  assault / hangar-falls lose state stay deferred to `AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK`. The
  B7 timing harness's `rush` plan is pinned as a legal play sequence by test.

Evidence: full suite green at `dev` HEAD `72ac25b32` (9253 tests, 411 files);
`npm run build` clean; GDD §8.2 Rule-2 and ring/playstyle sections updated.
EPIC AC5 is per-hex: **every** weapon-granting hex's boss demonstrates its
grant (the ring's own weapon hex and the shipped weapon upgrades).

# Intake brief — Timed consumable field pickups should use the absorbed-hit model (AH-0MVUVSW4J0009QUW)

**Type:** feature · **Priority:** medium · **Discovered from:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW ·
**Blocked by:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (dependency edge, parent plan `plan_complete`)

**Producer decisions (2026-10-30):** Q-A1 = **b** (a pickup's charge does **not**
regenerate — one drop buys one event, then the item is inert) · Q-A2 = **a**
(temporary-level TTL reuses today's windows: Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force
Field 8 s) · Q-A3 = **resolved** (AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P is not delivered
separately). See [Decisions](#decisions-producer-2026-10-30).

## Headline

A **field pickup** of Shield, Thorn Field or Force Field should buy **one charge
of one event** (one absorbed hit / one free ram / one reflected bullet) from the
shared consumable charge pool that AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW introduces, instead of
opening a level-resolved **timed window** — and that pickup charge is **not
backed by regeneration**, so a single drop is worth exactly one event. The three
per-kind window axes retire and their level curves re-point at the charge cap /
regeneration interval, so a pickup and a hold-full grant share one model, one
HUD row and one code path, differing only in whether the pool refills.

## Original seed (as filed)

Convert the **timed field pickups** of the budget/consumable power-ups (Shield,
Thorn Field, Force Field) to the same one-event charge model the permanent
consumable pool uses, so a pickup spends a single event (one absorbed hit / one
free ram / one reflected bullet) instead of opening a timed window.

Produced by the producer's answer to **Q2** on AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (*Consumable
upgrades should not be endless*): one charge buys one single event (option b),
and the timed-pickup conversion is deliberately split into this follow-up so that
change lands after the permanent-charge model.

## Problem statement

The run-scoped model now has **two contradictory shapes for the same item**. A
hold-full grant of Shield/Thorn Field/Force Field becomes a **charge pool** (one
event per charge, level-derived cap and regeneration, HUD countdown —
AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW), while a **field pickup** of the same item still opens a
**level-resolved timed window** with its own parallel budget counter and its own
HUD countdown. The player sees "one absorbed hit" from one acquisition path and
"up to 18 seconds of cover" from the other, and the effect path keeps two
mechanisms (window + budget) for what the design calls one thing.

## Users

- **The player** who collects Shield / Thorn Field / Force Field from a drop and
  wants the same legible "one hit, then it comes back" behaviour they get from a
  hold-full grant — not a timer that means a different thing per acquisition
  path.
- **The balance owner**, who needs one bounded unit of value ("one absorbed
  hit") with one level axis pair (cap + regeneration) instead of a window
  duration that silently changes how many events the same pickup buys.
- **The maintainer**, who wants the window machinery deleted rather than
  parallel-cased for three kinds.

**User stories**

- "As a player, when I collect a Shield drop I get **one** absorbed hit — not a
  15-second bubble — and the HUD row tells me when the next absorption is due."
- "As a player, when I collect Thorn Field I get **one** free ram, and when I
  collect Force Field I get **one** reflected bullet; each of them recharges on
  the same rhythm the hold-full version uses."
- "As a balance owner, the three kinds have exactly two level axes each — a
  charge cap and a regeneration interval — and no window duration that changes
  the number of events a pickup is worth."

## Desired change

1. A **field pickup** (`applyCollect(id, false)`) of `shield`, `thorns` or
   `force_field` grants **exactly one charge** into the shared consumable charge
   pool AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW introduces (clamped at the level-resolved cap) and
   **opens no effect window**. The pickup still adds its existing **one
   temporary level stack** (field-pickup levelling is unchanged — the temporary
   stack raises the cap/interval while it lasts and reverts on its own TTL,
   which the sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A supplies); charges already granted
   are **never clawed back** when that TTL expires (AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC
   resolved decision 2).
2. **A pickup-granted charge does not regenerate (producer decision Q-A1=b).**
   A single drop buys **exactly one event** and the item is **inert afterwards**:
   no charge is banked back for a consumable the player only ever picked up.
   Regeneration is gated on **permanent ownership** — the pool's regenerating
   ceiling for these three kinds is `permanentGrants(id) > 0 ? cap : 0`, so an
   item that was never a hold-full grant never refills on its own. The gate is
   **catalogue data** (a consumable property alongside the parent's `consumable`
   flag), not a per-kind `id === …` special case, and it is **scoped to these
   three kinds**: the shipped regenerating behaviour of Phase Shift / Teleport
   field pickups (AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT) is unchanged.
3. **One charge = one event**, spent through the existing shared consumption
   seams with no new counter: `tryAbsorbShield()` spends one charge (one
   absorbed hit), `tryConsumeThornsRam()` spends one charge (one free ram),
   `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` spends one charge (one reflected bullet).
   The registry-local `_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` /
   `_forceFieldRemaining` counters are replaced by pool-derived accessors, so
   there is one source of truth per kind.
4. **Armed means "holds a charge"** — the bubble/aura is drawn while the pool
   has at least one charge and pops when the last charge is spent (the existing
   pop-on-last-absorb path), so the final-second wind-down animation of the
   timed window has no trigger left for Shield and must be either re-pointed at
   the TTL or documented as retired (dead-code decision recorded, not silently
   dropped).
5. **The three window axes retire.** `shieldDuration`, `thornsDuration` and
   `forceFieldDuration` are removed from `PowerUpLevelVariable`,
   `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` and
   `PowerUpLevelStats`; no replacement window axis is introduced. The three
   kinds keep exactly two axes each — the parent's charge cap and regeneration
   interval (`shieldAbsorptions` + new `shieldRecharge`; `thornsAbsorbs` +
   `thornsRecharge`; `forceFieldReflects` + new `forceFieldRecharge`).
6. **The per-kind window TTL resolver must be updated with the retirement.** The
   sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A resolves a temporary-window TTL per kind
   (timed kinds → their level-resolved effect duration, instant kinds → a
   declared `temporaryWindow` value). After this change these three kinds are
   **instant kinds** for that resolver, so they declare flat `temporaryWindow`
   values (producer decision Q-A2=a) and must not be read through
   `stats.shieldDuration` / `stats.thornsDuration` /
   `stats.forceFieldDuration`.
7. **HUD** — after a pickup these three kinds show the charge count on the
   shared consumable row and **no window countdown**; because a pickup-only
   charge never regenerates, the row shows **no regeneration countdown** either
   (there is nothing to count down), is greyed while owned-and-empty, and
   disappears once the temporary-level TTL expires (the existing field-only
   rule). A **permanently granted** item keeps the parent's full behaviour (live
   `next in Ns` countdown, greyed empty row). The parent's HUD work
   (AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6) owns the rendering; this item owns the assertion that a
   **pickup** lands in the right row state, and removes the Thorn-specific
   `_powerUpRecharge` special case in favour of the shared consumable path.
8. **Parity** — every change lands in the shared core
   (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) so `PlayScene` and every gym that spawns or
   consumes these kinds inherit it; the duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` assertions stay green, and the parity matrix rows for
   these kinds are updated where the retained divergences change.

### Per-kind conversion table

| Kind | Today (field pickup) | After (field pickup) |
|---|---|---|
| Shield | 15 s → 30 s bubble + 1 → 3 absorptions, refreshed on re-collect | 1 charge = **1 absorbed hit**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `shieldAbsorptions` (1 → 3) and regeneration `shieldRecharge` (45 s → shorter) only once the item is permanently owned; temporary level TTL **15 s** |
| Thorn Field | 8 s → 16 s window + 2 → 6 rams, refilled every 12 s → 5 s *while the window is open* | 1 charge = **1 free ram**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `thornsAbsorbs` (2 → 6) and regeneration `thornsRecharge` (12 s → 5 s) only once permanently owned; temporary level TTL **8 s** |

So a drop is worth exactly **one event** (the producer's Q-A1=b scarcity rule), while a
hold-full grant keeps the parent's regenerating pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — A pickup grants exactly one charge and no effect window.** A Shield /
  Thorn Field / Force Field field pickup adds exactly one charge to the shared
  consumable pool, clamped at the level-resolved cap, and opens no effect
  window: no `shieldDuration` / `thornsDuration` / `forceFieldDuration` read
  remains on the path, and the registry's timed map never holds these ids after
  a pickup. It still adds its one temporary level stack. Tests assert pool count
  and clamp per kind, the absence of a window, and that the temporary-stack TTL
  expiry leaves the granted charge intact (no clawback).
- **AC2 — One charge resolves exactly one event and a pickup charge never
  regenerates.** Each spent charge resolves exactly one event (Shield one
  absorbed hit, Thorn Field one free ram, Force Field one reflected bullet); a
  **pickup-only** item then stays empty and **inert** — no regeneration clock
  starts, and a long tick grants nothing (`permanentGrants(id) === 0` ⇒
  regenerating ceiling 0). A **permanently granted** item keeps the parent's
  spend→empty→regenerate→re-use cycle. Both cycles are asserted per kind, in
  `PlayScene`'s shared core and in a gym, with no duplicate counter left behind
  (`_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` / `_forceFieldRemaining` removed or
  derived); a regression test pins that Phase Shift / Teleport pickup
  regeneration is unchanged.
- **AC3 — HUD shows the pickup charge with no countdown that cannot happen.**
  After a field pickup the kind's HUD row shows the charge count and **no**
  regeneration or window countdown (a pickup-only charge never regenerates), the
  row is greyed while empty and disappears when the temporary-level TTL expires;
  a permanently granted item's row keeps the parent's live `next in Ns`
  countdown and greyed-empty state. HUD tests cover each state per kind and
  assert that a pickup row never renders a countdown it cannot honour, and the
  Thorn-specific `_powerUpRecharge` case is replaced by the shared consumable
  path.
- **AC4 — The window axes are retired, not orphaned.** `shieldDuration`,
  `thornsDuration` and `forceFieldDuration` are absent from
  `PowerUpLevelVariable`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` and
  `PowerUpLevelStats`, with no remaining reference in `src/` outside tests that
  assert their removal; the change-summary/deferred-axis seam
  (`DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`) stays consistent, and the per-kind
  temporary-window TTL resolver classifies the three kinds as instant kinds with
  the producer-approved flat values — **Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force
  Field 8 s** (coordinated with AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A).
- **AC4b — The no-regeneration gate is catalogue data, not a special case.**
  The "a pickup charge does not regenerate until the item is permanently owned"
  rule is expressed as a consumable property in `src/powerups/types.ts` and read
  by the store/registry; no `id === 'shield' | 'thorns' | 'force_field'` branch
  appears outside the catalogue, and the gate is scoped so Phase Shift / Teleport
  pickup regeneration is unchanged (regression-tested).
- **AC5 — Game and gym behave identically.** All behaviour runs through the
  shared store/registry/`CombatScene` seams; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`

- **AC6 — Checkpoint resume is unchanged and singled out.** A pickup-earned
  charge is not persisted and no window re-opens on resume (existing rule,

- **AC7 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4

## Constraints

- **Must land after AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW.** The shared charge pool, the
  charge/regeneration accessors and the HUD row work are that item's; this item
  consumes them and must not implement a parallel pool.
- **No parallel implementation.** One pool, one grant path, one spend path per
  kind — the shared store/registry seams, never a per-scene copy.
- **No rebalance beyond the model.** Do not change the shipped caps
  (`shieldAbsorptions` 1 → 3, `thornsAbsorbs` 2 → 6, `forceFieldReflects`
  3 → 10) or the parent's regeneration curves; the only value changes are the
  retired window axes and the producer-approved temporary-level TTLs (Shield
  15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force Field 8 s).
- **Scarcity rule (Q-A1=b).** A pickup-granted charge is worth **one event** and
  never refills unless the item is permanently owned; do not soften this into a
  token regeneration "just for pickups", and do not extend the rule to Phase
  Shift / Teleport, whose shipped pickup regeneration (AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT) is
  unchanged.
- **No clawback.** Charges already granted survive a temporary-level TTL
  expiry (AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC resolved decision 2).
- **Coordinate with in-flight work on the same surface:**
  - AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P (*Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance — the drop is now much weaker (high, resolution safety-critical).**
  Under Q-A1=b a Force Field drop buys **one** reflection (today: 3–10 inside
  8–18 s) and a Thorn Field drop buys **one** ram (today: 2–6 inside 8–16 s).
  This is the producer's chosen scarcity, but it is a visible nerf to two
  popular drops and could make them read as broken in play. Mitigations: the
  granted charge **persists until used** (no window to waste), the cap axes are
  unchanged, and the change should be watched with the existing balance/eval
  harness; if it proves too weak the fix is a catalogue/level change, not a
  code change.
- **Consumable-consistency (medium).** After this change Shield / Thorn Field /
  Force Field pickups do **not** regenerate while Phase Shift / Teleport pickups
  do. That asymmetry is deliberate (Q-A1=b, scoped to the three converted
  kinds) but is exactly the sort of split that gets "normalised" by a later
  refactor, so AC4b/AC2 pin it with regression tests and the docs state the
  reason.
- **Dead-code/coupling (medium).** Retiring three catalogue axes removes the
  read path another in-flight item's TTL resolver leans on
  (AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A) and a Shield wind-down animation whose trigger
  disappears. Both must be handled explicitly (AC4, Desired change 4), not left
  as broken references.
- **HUD/slot semantics (medium).** These kinds leave the "timed window" class, so
  the F5 (AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M) premises around row countdown and slot release at
  window expiry no longer hold; the temporary *level* now expires on its own TTL
  while the charge persists — a combination no existing test covers today.
- **Test churn (medium).** `shieldDuration` / `thornsDuration` /
  `forceFieldDuration` appear across `effects.test.ts`,
  `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `temporaryRevert.test.ts` and `HUD.test.ts`; the
  window assertions must be rewritten as charge-cycle assertions rather than
  deleted, or the coverage for these kinds silently drops.
- **Scope creep (low).** The conversion invites "why not Frenzy/Chrono/Salvage
  too?" and "why doesn't my pickup refill?" — both deliberately out of scope
  (recorded as linked work, not expanded here).
- **Assumption A1.** A field pickup of these kinds still adds **one temporary
  level stack** (keeping today's levelling), so repeated pickups raise the cap
  for the run; the level TTL is the producer-approved flat value from the
  sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A, not a level curve (the duration axes that
  used to grow it are retired).
- **Assumption A2.** "Opens no timed window" refers to the **effect** window
  (the 8–18 s bubble/aura), not the temporary-*level* TTL; the two are distinct
  concepts and both can be true at once.
- **Assumption A3.** The HUD needs no new widget — the parent's `next in Ns`
  formatter and greyed-empty-row rules cover these kinds; this item only proves
  the pickup path reaches that state (and renders no countdown when nothing
  regenerates).
- **Assumption A6.** The Q-A1=b gate means "regenerating ceiling = cap when
  permanently owned, 0 otherwise" — a single derived number, not a second
  charge counter, and it is scoped to the three converted kinds so Phase
  Shift / Teleport pickup regeneration is untouched.
- **Assumption A7.** Because the duration axes retire, the temporary-level TTL
  is **flat** (no longer level-derived); a levelled item's temporary stack no
  longer lasts longer than a level-0 one. Recorded as an intentional
  consequence of Q-A2=a (`a` was chosen to preserve today's *level-0* window
  length).
- **Assumption A4.** A pickup grants **one** charge regardless of the resolved
  cap (the cap only bounds banking), so the conversion cannot be a stealth buff
  to a fresh pickup.
- **Assumption A5.** Checkpoint persistence is unaffected: pickup grants are
  temporary (not replayed), permanent grants are replayed — unchanged from
  today.

2026-10-30 (recorded as decisions D1–D3 and in the Appendix). Two interpretation
consequences are recorded as assumptions rather than re-asked, because they
follow directly from the answers and from the code:

- **A6 (from D1).** The gate is implemented as a derived "regenerating ceiling"
  per kind (cap when permanently owned, 0 otherwise) instead of a second charge
  counter or a per-kind `id === …` branch, and it applies only to the three
  converted kinds.
- **A7 (from D2).** The temporary-level TTL is now flat rather than
  level-derived, because the duration curves it used to follow are retired.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q-A1 — Ownership/regeneration after a field pickup.**
  - Options: (a) yes — same pool and ownership as a hold-full grant (matches
    today's Phase Shift / Teleport pickups); (b) no — one charge, no
    regeneration, item inert afterwards; (c) freeform. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): "b"** — a field pickup grants **one charge
    that is not backed by regeneration**; a single drop buys exactly one event
    and the item stays inert afterwards. Source: interactive reply. Recorded as
    **decision D1**; implementation interpretation recorded as assumption A6.
- **Q-A2 — Temporary-level TTL for the three kinds.**
  - Options: (a) reuse today's level-0 window (Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s,
    Force Field 8 s); (b) uniform 15 s like the other instant kinds; (c)
    freeform. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): "a"** — reuse the current windows. Source:
    interactive reply. Recorded as **decision D2**; the flat-TTL consequence is
    recorded as assumption A7.
- **Q-A3 — Is AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P closed or re-scoped?**
  - Asked as: *"Decide whether AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P (Permanent Force Field
    regenerate budget) is closed or re-scoped, since its remaining scope is
    subsumed by this item."*
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): "yes"** — i.e. do not deliver it
    separately. Source: interactive reply. Interpreted conservatively as
    **re-scope now, close after this item and the parent ship** (D3): closing a
    still-blocked item today would lose the requirement if the parent's scope
    changes, which is the same rule the parent's plan applied to
    AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP.
- **Q-A4 (agent, technical — answered by code evidence, no producer needed).**
  *Must the window axes be retired or merely excluded?* Answer (eng): **retired**
  — the parent's AC4 asks for no dead axes, and the three axes are read only by
  `_applyTimedEffect` for these kinds (`src/powerups/effects.ts:535/592/636`),
  so removal is contained. A `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` exclusion stays
  as the documented fallback only if a consumer is found that cannot be removed
  in this change.
- **Q-A5 (agent, technical — answered by code evidence).** *Does the change need
  a new counter for "remaining absorptions", or a second counter for
  pickup-vs-permanent charges?* Answer (eng): **neither** — the pool count is
  the remaining budget, and D1's gate is a derived regenerating ceiling, so
  `_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` / `_forceFieldRemaining` collapse into
  the parent's pool accessors (AC2, AC4b).

## Review notes (five mini-review stages)

1. **Completeness** — problem, users, ACs, constraints, existing state, desired
   change, key files all present; the retired-axis consumer (TTL resolver) and
   the no-regeneration gate were added as explicit ACs (AC4, AC4b) after the
   related-work pass and the producer answers.
2. **Capture fidelity** — the producer's answers are represented verbatim
   (Q-A1 = "b", Q-A2 = "a", Q-A3 = "yes") with the interpretation of each
   recorded as a named decision/assumption, including the one genuinely
   ambiguous answer (Q-A3, "yes" to "closed or re-scoped").
3. **Related-work & traceability** — parent plan children (F2/F3/F4/F7), the

4. **Risks & assumptions** — six risks with mitigations, seven assumptions;

   the scope-creep risk are recorded.
5. **Polish & handoff** — UK English, file paths with line evidence,

# Goal

As a player, I want my hangar and my ring to survive closing the browser, so
that hours of salvage are never lost, and as a maintainer I want one versioned,
corrupt-safe `localStorage` key so a defence result can never be written without
the hangar state it depends on.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase A. This
is the persistence foundation every other hangar/ring item reads and writes
through.

## Context

- GDD §6.6 save-data rules: `localStorage` only, defensive parse, no backend,
  injectable storage.
- Precedents: `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` (v2 payload, `CHECKPOINT_STORAGE_KEY`,
  injectable `CheckpointStorage`, defensive parse → `null`, field-presence
  migration), `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/core/settingsStore.ts`,
  `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`.
- The shipped keys are `ai_hell_leaderboard`, `ai_hell_settings`,
  `ai_hell_checkpoint` and `ai_hell_lastSession`; this item adds the fifth,
  `ai_hell_hangar_war`.
- Payload sketch (design of record, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D
  § Persistence and save model): `version`, `seed`, `hangar`
  (`bankedMinerals`, `bankedCores`, `unlockedHulls`, `unlockedWeapons`,
  `ownedModifiers`, `activeHull`, `activeLoadout`), `ring` (`ringIndex`,
  `hexes[]` with axial `q`/`r`, `held`, `aggression`, `defender`,
  `bossDefeated`, `grantedWeapon`), `pendingAttacks`, `bestScore`.

## Scope

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`: `HANGAR_WAR_STORAGE_KEY`,
  `HANGAR_WAR_VERSION`, the typed payload, load/save through an injectable
  `HangarWarStorage` (localStorage by default), `createDefaultPayload(seed)`.
- Defensive parse: corrupt JSON, wrong shape, unknown version or out-of-range
  values load as `null` or as the last valid hangar state with an empty ring —
  never throw, never discard a partial ring.
- Field-presence migration so an older hangar-only save loads as "hangar at its
  last valid state, empty ring", stamped with the current version on parse.
- A migration note in the module docblock.

## Tests first

Table-driven corrupt/partial/legacy payload tests before the parser; round-trip
and injection tests before the store API.

## Key Files

- new: `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` (+ test)
- reference: `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`, `src/core/settingsStore.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on the test harness (A1) for the storage fake and fixtures.
- Blocks salvage banking (A3), the hangar economy (A4) and the ring model (B2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Persistence.** One versioned `localStorage` key for hangar + ring under GDD
  §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend, injectable store), with a migration
  note; a partial ring is never discarded.
- Corrupt JSON, wrong-shape payloads, unknown versions and out-of-range values
  never throw and never wipe a valid hangar: each case has a table-driven test.
- A hangar-only (pre-ring) payload loads with the hangar intact and an empty
  ring, and a partial ring round-trips unchanged.
- Storage is injected in every test (no direct `localStorage` access in the
  module's unit tests), and `npm run build` plus the changed-scope gate pass.

# Goal

As a player, I want the salvage I earn to be banked at the run's checkpoint
moments, so that reaching a mid-run milestone means something for my fleet and a
later death only costs me what I had not banked yet.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase A. This
is the persistent echo of the shipped in-run mineral economy.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, *States* —
  "a bad run still banks salvage from the checkpoints it reached"; "losing a run
  never does this [hangar falls]: the run's unbanked salvage is forfeit, the
  hangar and the ring survive".
- The run economy (minerals, the hold, levelling) is **unchanged**; salvage is
  its persistent echo, banked at the existing checkpoint moments (mini-boss
  defeats — see `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` and where `saveCheckpoint` is
  called from `PlayScene`).
- Mini-boss cores are the second currency (epic AC1).
- The fleet starts minimal but the **run** keeps the shipped six shared loadout
  slots plus Extra Life and Mystery UFO; nothing here strips the run.

## Scope

- Pure `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts`: `bankSalvage(banked, runSalvage)`
  and `runSalvageFromRun(...)` (minerals held/earned + mini-boss cores),
  idempotent per checkpoint, with explicit "unbanked is forfeit on death"
  semantics.
- Wire the banking call at the existing checkpoint seam in the shared run code —
  the same code path for the arcade run and a hex deployment, no divergent copy.
- Persist the banked balance through the hangar-war store.

## Tests first

Pure-module table tests (bank at each checkpoint moment, repeated banking
idempotence, forfeiture on death) before wiring; a scene-level test asserts the
banked balance rises at a mini-boss defeat and not on a death before it.

- new: `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` (+ test)

  ring's hardest hex").

# Goal

As a player, I want the AI frontier to feel like a real opponent I can always
answer: between runs its aggression rises and it may attack a hex I hold, and a
defending bot either holds the line or loses it by a rule I can read — not by an
opaque simulated battle.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § New systems
  required ("**Algorithmic defence resolution** — a taken hex falls or holds by
  comparing stored numbers (defender rating vs. attacking force × aggression) —
  **no simulated battle**"; "**Frontier aggression clock** — each between-run
  tick raises border aggression and lets the AI attack a held hex, retaking it
  unless the player defeats the attacking neighbour first").
- Failure mode to design against: *the frontier treadmill* and *opaque defence* —
  mitigation is an answerable tick and numbers the player can see.
- Producer decision 2026-10-30, Q2 = a: no massed hangar assault and no
  hangar-falls lose state in this build (`AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK` tracks those).

## Scope

- Pure `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`: `resolveDefence({defenderRating,
  attackingForce, aggression, seed})` → hold/fall, and `runFrontierTick(state)`
  → next state plus a structured per-tick record (hex, attacking force,
  aggression, attacker origin, outcome, margin) consumed by the defence report
  (B6).
- Defender rating comes from the defending hull's hangar upgrades (A4), never a
  live battle; the defending bot is never flown.
- Deterministic from the stored `seed` + injectable clock, so a replay reproduces
  every hold and fall.
- Aggression growth per tick is data-driven and answerable: attacker origin is
  the neighbouring hex the player can strike back at.

## Tests first

Table-driven resolver tests (defender ahead, attacker ahead, exact tie, aggression
scaling, seeded jitter bounds) and tick-sequence replay tests before the code.

## Key Files

- new: `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` (+ test), optional
  `src/data/frontier-tuning.json` for tick constants
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B2 (ring model) and A4 (defender rating).
- Prerequisite for the capture cycle (B5) and the defence report (B6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Algorithmic defence + frontier tick.** A pure resolver decides holds/falls from
  stored numbers (defender rating vs attacking force × aggression), with no
  simulated battle, returning a structured per-tick record that the defence
  report (B6) renders as the numbers behind every result.
- One frontier tick between runs raises border aggression and can retake a held
  hex; the tick is deterministic from the stored seed and uses an injectable
  clock, and it names the attacking neighbour so the player can answer it.
- Unit tests cover holds, falls, retakes, a defence that is outmatched, the
  aggression scaling and full replay determinism from the same seed and payload.
- No hangar assault and no hangar-falls lose state are introduced (Q2 = a),
  asserted by a test that a completed ring opens the next ring without a
  hangar-defence pass.

# Goal

As a player, I want taking a hex to be a normal run at that hex's aggression,
ending on its boss, and — when I win — to bank the salvage, receive the hex's
weapon or upgrade into my hangar, and leave a bot flying a hull of mine to hold
it; and I want the ring to be secured when every hex of it is held.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B. This is
the capture cycle, the heart of the outer loop.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Loop structure
  (the capture cycle) and § Progression rules Rule 2 — "the boss wields it first".
- Producer decisions: **Q2 = a** — "ring secured = every hex of the current ring
  held"; the massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state are deferred
  to `AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK`. **Q3 = a** — ring 2 opens and is playable.
- Rule 1 clarification: the fleet starts minimal, but the **run** keeps the
  shipped six shared loadout slots plus Extra Life and Mystery UFO unchanged.
- Prior children: A3 (banking), A4 (economy/defender rating), A6 (deployment
  path), B2 (ring), B3 (resolver), B4 (map).

## Scope

- Hex deployment: `PlayScene` at the hex's aggression-selected difficulty, ending
  in the hex boss (a boss variant on the shared boss path, never a copy).
- Boss victory resolution: bank the salvage, mark the hex held and
  `bossDefeated`, grant the hex's weapon/upgrade entry into the hangar (Rule 2 —
  the boss demonstrates it first; the entry is purchasable afterwards), apply the
  pre-run combat variants the boss demonstrated where the shipped boss path
  supports it.
- Leave-a-bot step: choose a hull, record `defender` (hull id, derived defence
  rating) in the payload; a hex cannot be held without a defender.
- Ring-secured detection: every hex of the current ring held → ring secured, the
  next ring opens. No hangar assault pass (Q2 = a).

## Tests first

Capture-cycle state-machine tests (win → bank → grant → defend, loss → unbanked
forfeit, hex not held without a defender, ring-secured at the last hex, ring 2
opens) in the gym/headless harness before the scene wiring.

## Key Files

- new: `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (+ test), a hex-boss variant on the
  shared boss path, capture/deployment wiring in `src/scenes/`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B4 (map/deployment), B3 (defence rating), A4 (grants), A6 (launch
  isolation).
- Prerequisite for the defence report (B6) and timing validation (B7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capture cycle.** Taking a hex = a normal run at that hex's aggression, ending
  in the hex boss; defeating the boss banks salvage, grants the hex's weapon or
  upgrade into the hangar, and lets the player leave a bot flying a chosen hull.
  **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held** (producer decision
  2026-10-30, Q2 = a); the massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state
  are deferred (AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK).
- **Boss-granted discovery.** A hex boss demonstrates the weapon it grants; the
  entry appears in the hangar only after the boss is defeated (Rule 2), with the
  six-slot, Extra Life and Mystery UFO behaviour of the shipped run unchanged
  (Rule 1 clarification).
- A hex cannot be marked held without a defender, and the defender's stored rating
  derives from the chosen hull's hangar upgrades — both asserted by tests.
- Securing the last hex of a ring opens the next ring (ring 2 playable) without a
  hangar assault pass.

# Goal

As a player, I want a between-sortie defence report that tells me which of my
hexes were attacked, which held and which fell, and the exact numbers behind each
result — and as a demo watcher I never want attract mode to stall on a defence or
on a new screen.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § UI / scene
  surface (the between-sortie defence report) and § Attract mode ("the bot
  traverses or skips every new screen — on the map it auto-picks the **weakest**
  adjacent hex, in the hangar it auto-buys the cheapest useful unlock, and it
  auto-advances the defence report. Because defence is resolved algorithmically,
  there is no live defence battle for the demo to stall in").
- Failure modes to mitigate: *opaque defence* ("a hex falls and the player cannot
  see why … show the numbers (defender rating vs. attacking force)") and *the
  frontier treadmill* (an answerable tick, shown).
- Today there is no scene-to-scene menu traversal in demo mode — the demo boots
  straight into `PlayScene` — so the traversal here is new behaviour
  (`src/ai/`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`).

## Scope

- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts`: per-hex rows from the resolver's per-tick
  record — attacking force, aggression, defender rating, outcome, margin, and
  what it would take to retake the hex — plus a continue action back to the map.
- Frontier tick integration: the tick runs between runs (on returning from a
  deployment) and its record feeds this screen.
- Attract-mode traversal for the whole new surface: menu → map → (weakest hex)
  deployment → defence report → map → hangar (cheapest useful unlock), driven by
  pure, tested bot decisions with seeded choices; no live defence battle exists to
  stall in.

## Tests first

Report-rendering tests from a synthetic tick record and a full traversal
integration test (bot drives every new screen without stalling) before the scene
and bot wiring.

## Key Files

- new: `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` (+ test), traversal decisions in
  `src/ai/` (+ tests)
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B3 (tick record), B5 (between-run wiring) and A5 (hangar).
- Prerequisite for timing validation (B7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The defence report shows the numbers that produced every result: per hex the
  attacking force, aggression, defender rating, hold/fall outcome, margin and what
  it would take to retake it, generated from the resolver's per-tick record.
- **Attract mode never stalls.** The demo bot traverses or skips the map, hangar
  and defence report (auto-pick weakest hex, auto-buy cheapest useful unlock) and
  there is no live defence battle to stall in.
- An integration test drives menu → map → deployment → defence report → map →
  hangar with the bot and asserts every screen advances within a bounded time and
  no defence battle is ever simulated.
- The report is a pure view over the tick record and the stored payload — the same
  code path runs in `GymHexWar`, with no gameplay rule in the scene.

# Goal

As the producer, I want the ring's play time and playstyle trade-off measured
rather than guessed — ring 1 at 40–60 minutes and ring 2 at ≈70–100 minutes for a
semi-skilled player, with the rush line faster-but-riskier and the grind line
safer-but-slower — so the ring lands as an evening's play and neither strategy is
strictly dominant.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Session shape
  ("the **one-ring MVP targets 40–60 minutes** … **Ring 2 is larger — 12 hexes** —
  so it lands at … **≈70–100 minutes**") and § Playstyles supported ("No style is
  strictly dominant — the aggressive line is **faster but riskier** and slow
  grinding is **safer but slower**, which is the intended trade").
- Intake assumption A1: timing is measured with the existing headless eval arena —
  `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` reports per-run `durationSeconds` / `ticksSimulated`, so
  a ring's play time is summed from simulated deployments rather than guessed. No
  new instrumentation is required.
- Intake assumption Q4: the headless arena is sufficient evidence for the
  recorded target; a human playtest is desirable but not a gate.

## Scope

- A headless ring-timing harness (a thin driver over `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) that
  simulates a ring's deployments at their resolved aggression and sums
  `durationSeconds`, plus a modelled build/retry allowance so the budget covers
  the whole ring rather than deployments alone.
- Two strategy simulations: **rush** (weapon hex first, then push into the next
  ring) and **grind** (secure the ring before pushing); record deployments,
  losses, salvage and wall-clock minutes for each.
- Tuning of aggression growth, defender ratings and grant strengths so both
  budgets and both strategies land in range; record the measured numbers,
  method and confidence in the GDD §8 timings section (B8 writes the prose; this
  item supplies the numbers) and on the work item.
- Any budget miss beyond tolerance raises a child item rather than silently
  widening the target.

## Tests first

A deterministic timing-harness test (same seed → same summed duration) and a
budget-assertion test with an explicit tolerance before tuning.

## Key Files

- new: `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` (+ test / CLI entry), ring timing fixtures
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`,
  `src/data/frontier-tuning.json`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B6 (the whole ring loop, including the between-run tick).
- Prerequisite for the docs item (B8).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Timing targets.** One-ring MVP is completable in 40–60 minutes by a
  semi-skilled player; ring 2 (12 hexes) lands at ≈70–100 minutes; the timing is
  recorded in the GDD and measured with the headless eval arena
  (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` per-run durations, summed per ring).
- **Playstyles supported.** A rush through the weapon hex into the next ring, and
  a full grind of the ring before pushing, are both viable and neither is strictly
  dominant; the difficulty curve makes the aggressive line riskier but faster.
- The timing harness is deterministic (same seed and payload → same summed
  duration, asserted by a test) and a budget test asserts both ring windows with a
  stated tolerance.
- The measured numbers, strategy comparison and method are recorded on the work
  item for the docs item to publish.

As a player, I want the hex boss to **use** the weapon it grants me against me before I can earn it, so that "the boss wields it first" (Rule 2) is something I experience rather than a colour I have to infer.

Closes the **AC5 gap** found by the audit of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (2026-11-01): the grant is correctly gated on boss defeat, but the demonstration is only a body-colour cue (`src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts:16`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3134`) rather than the boss wielding the weapon.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, progression Rule 2 — "The boss wields it first": a hex boss demonstrates the hex's new weapon or power-up against the player.
- The hex boss is a **variant** on the shipped `Boss` path, never a copy: `src/entities/Boss.ts` exposes `BossConfig` hooks (`bodyColor`, `desperationColor`, `phaseCount`, `hitPointsPerPhase`) and a `firePhase()` override seam that `MiniBoss` already uses for config-driven pattern sets.
- The shared weapon catalogue `src/utils/weapons.ts` carries each weapon's fan pattern (relative radian offsets), fire interval, bullet colour and speed signature; the demonstration must be **derived from that catalogue** (no second weapon table).
- Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md): the demonstration runs in the shipped `Boss` consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym; no gym-only branch, no copied body (the `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` guard stays green).

## Scope

- Add a default-preserving `BossConfig` hook for a **demonstrated weapon** and have the boss open the encounter by firing that weapon's volley (fan pattern, colour, speed) instead of its shipped phase-1 pattern; subsequent phases keep the shipped patterns unchanged.
- Resolve the demo descriptor in the pure hex-boss module (`src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts`) from the target hex's authored grant and the shared weapon catalogue, and expose it on `HexBossProfile` so `PlayScene`, the gyms and tests all read one source.
- Keep a hex with no weapon grant (upgrade-only hex, unknown hex) exactly as today (no demo, shipped patterns).
- Document the demonstration in the module docblock and GDD §8.2 (the "wields it first" sentence now describes real behaviour).

## Out of scope

- Player-side exotic mechanics on boss bullets (wave-laser damage budget, edge bouncing, cluster split): the demonstration is the weapon's volley (pattern/colour/speed), not a second implementation of the player bullet system.
- Changing the shipped classic campaign boss (no config = byte-for-byte unchanged behaviour).

Pure profile tests (grant → demo descriptor, upgrade-only hex → no demo, unknown hex → no demo, descriptor derived from the weapon catalogue) and entity tests through the public `Boss`/`HexBoss` API (the demo volley fires on the opening phase, later phases keep shipped patterns, a plain boss never fires a demo volley) before the implementation.

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` (config hook + open-encounter volley), `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts` (+ test)

- Tests cover: grant → demo descriptor derived from the catalogue; the opening phase fires the demo volley with that pattern/colour; later phases keep the shipped patterns; no-demo configs fire the shipped pattern.

# Goal

As a player who wants to play aggressively, I want to take a ring's hardest (weapon) hex and then **push into the next ring while the rest of this ring is still unheld**, so that the rush line the timing budget and the GDD advertise is an actual choice with a real cost — not a run I cannot play.

Closes the **AC8 gap** found by the audit of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (2026-11-01): `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts:430-438` models a rush that takes the weapon hex and pushes into the next ring leaving the rest exposed, but `openNextRing` refuses until `isRingSecured` (every hex held — `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:347-352`), so the modelled strategy is unreachable in play.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, agreed adjustment 3 — "Players may rush the hard hex and push into the next ring (risking losses) or grind the weaker hexes and secure the ring first — **different play styles must all be viable**".
- Producer decision Q2 = a remains intact: **ring secured = every hex of the current ring held** (no massed hangar assault, no hangar-falls lose state — `AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK`). "Secured" stays the *fully held* state; what changes is that ring **advance** no longer requires it.
- Today the payload holds one ring (`HangarWarPayload.ring`, `HexRingState.hexes`) and `openNextRing` **replaces** it; a rush would silently discard the hexes the player skipped, which contradicts "a partial ring is never discarded" (AC11) and removes the risk the design intends.
- Ring growth is data-driven (`ringSize(n) = 6n`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`), and exactly one hex per ring is the `weaponHex` — the ring's hardest, granting its new weapon (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`).

## Scope

- **Advance rule:** the next ring opens when the current ring's **capstone** hex (the ring's `weaponHex`, resolved from the authored definitions) is held. All-held (`isRingSecured`) remains the secured state and also opens the next ring; an unauthored/absent capstone falls back to the today's all-held rule.
- **Nothing discarded:** advancing carries the hexes the player skipped into the payload with their held state, defenders and aggression intact, so the rush keeps its cost and the frontier tick can still resolve their defence.
- `isRingSecured` becomes ring-scoped (every hex **of the current ring index** held) so the report/map keep meaning "this ring is secured" after growth.
- Ring growth stays data-driven (`ringSize(n) = 6n`); ring 2 remains playable and reachable by either line.
- Docs: GDD §8.2 rush/grind paragraph and the `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` docblock describe the now-reachable rush line; the timing baseline note records that the rush is playable.

## Out of scope

- Any change to Q2 = a (no hangar assault, no hangar-falls lose state).
- Re-tuning the measured timing budgets (B7's numbers stand; a regression test pins that the rush plan is now playable end-to-end).
- New UI beyond what the map/defence report already render (skipped hexes keep rendering through the existing intel path).

## Tests first

Capture-cycle tests (capstone held → next ring opens; ring secured still opens; skipped hexes retained with their state; unauthored capstone falls back to all-held; `isRingSecured` still false while a current-ring hex is unheld) and a timing-consistency test (the `rush` plan's deployments are a legal play sequence — after the weapon hex the next ring is openable) before the implementation.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (+ test), `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` (skipped-hex defence still resolves)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` (payload round-trip of carried hexes)
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` (+ test), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2

## Acceptance Criteria

- **The rush is playable:** holding the current ring's capstone (`weaponHex`) hex opens the next ring without holding the rest of the ring, and the ring-secured state (`isRingSecured`) still means every hex of the current ring is held (Q2 = a unchanged).
- Advancing never discards the skipped hexes: their held state, defenders and aggression survive in the payload, round-trip through the versioned store, and the frontier tick still resolves attacks on the held ones.
- Grinding still works: securing every hex of a ring also opens the next ring, and ring 2 remains playable from both lines.
- `isRingSecured` is ring-scoped, so the defence report and in-game "ring secured" status stay correct after a rush.
- Tests prove the rush sequence (capstone → next ring openable, skipped hexes retained and still defended) and that `ringTiming`'s rush plan is now a legal play sequence; the existing capture-cycle, store, defence and timing suites stay green.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass.
